table.brief: 12 narrow columns of short codes and numbers (monthly values Jan–Dec) plus a name column

understanding.purpose: Compare monthly mean ozone levels across six monitoring stations, revealing seasonal patterns and station-to-station differences.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a station in column 1, scan horizontally across months within that row, and compare stations vertically within a given month. The month columns form one chronological analytical sequence; the station column is the row key.
groups: Column 1 (Station): row identifier, should be visually distinct from the data field.
Columns 2–13 (Jan–Dec): one chronological sequence; can be read as quarters Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec.
keep_intact: All numeric values, including decimal points, on one line
may_wrap: None; all cells are short and should remain single-line. Wrapping station names would weaken row identification and scanning.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Refines r2A: Station 96→100px, all months stay 52px, using the full 724px measure. The 4px r2A left unused goes to the row key, which has the longest unbreakable content; months keep 3px slack. Avoids r2B's cramped 88px station and over-wide 53px months. Equal months are deliberate: the 12 months are one homogeneous sequence, and width-based quarter grouping is ambiguous with left-aligned headers and right-aligned numbers.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Keep r1A's uniform month band but rebalance: station 96 (14px breathing room around the 65px names, enough to read as a distinct key column) and all twelve months at exactly 52px. This removes the 52/53 stutter and stops the identifier column from eating slack that the numeric field needs. Totals 720px, 4px under budget as safety.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Sets a single rule: every column gets ~4px of internal slack on each side. Station drops from 110/128 to 90 (69px of text for the 65px longest word — just enough to stop it touching the rule), Jan and Dec get 52 because their content is 1px narrower, and the ten 28px months get 53. This fixes both r0A's dead left gutter and r0B's zero-slack edge months, and gives the numbers the same breathing room as the labels instead of less.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Test the opposite balance: shrink the station column to 88px (just 2px slack beyond the longest name) and give every month 53px, using the full 724px. Twelve equal month columns with 32px of text room make the numbers the most comfortable they can be; the trade-off is a tighter row key. Worth comparing directly against even-key.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: New allocation: Station 112px, all months 51px, still summing to 724px. This pushes row-key dominance further, giving the stub a generous buffer so each row reads as a unit, while the months stay equal and compact (2px slack). The trade-off is 1px less slack per month than even-100; choose this if station identification is the primary scanning task.

bad.name: r1B
bad.note: Keeps a deliberate hierarchy — the station column stays visibly the widest at 100px (79px of text, 14px of slack) so the row key anchors the left edge — but holds all twelve months at an identical 52px so the chronological sequence is perfectly even and each value gets 31px for 28px of digits. This is the r0A idea corrected: the label keeps its lead without stealing the numbers' margin, and the widths sum exactly to 724.
bad.why: December is 59px while every other month is 51px; the lone wide final column creates an arbitrary asymmetry that draws the eye away from the data and implies a distinction that does not exist.

bad.name: r1C
bad.note: New idea: use width itself to hint the quarter structure the reading notes call out. All months sit at 52px (31px of text) except Apr, Jul and Oct, which get 55px — a 3px extra gutter at each quarter boundary that groups Jan–Mar / Apr–Jun / Jul–Sep / Oct–Dec without adding any line or rule. Station is 91px so the labels keep a hair of slack rather than the exact-minimum 86 of r0C. If the quarter cue reads as noise, fall back to 'station-lead'.
bad.why: May, July and October are 55px while the other months are 52px; the periodic widening creates a false visual grouping and breaks the even rhythm needed to compare twelve equivalent months.

bad.name: r2C
bad.note: Salvage r1C's idea but anchor it correctly: widen only the last month of each quarter (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec at 56px) so the surplus white space sits between quarters as a soft gutter and never interrupts a quarter. Non-quarter-end months at 51px keep the sequence even, station at 90px stays clearly dominant. Pattern is now internally consistent (4 repeats, one rule) instead of 3 arbitrary bumps.
bad.why: March, June, September and December are 56px while the rest are 51px; the every-third-month emphasis is semantically meaningless and makes the numeric grid look irregular.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The station column consumes nearly a third of the table while each month gets only 44px—below the 49px minimum for a 28px value plus padding—so numbers crowd the borders or wrap, and the eye is pulled to empty space in the row-header column instead of across the monthly series.
bad.why: The station column consumes nearly a third of the table while each month gets only 44px—below the 49px minimum for a 28px value plus padding—so numbers crowd the borders or wrap, and the eye is pulled to empty space in the row-header column instead of across the monthly series.

rationale: This is a lookup-and-compare table: twelve equivalent monthly columns should share one width so the eye can sweep across a station's year without rhythmic interruptions. At 52px each month has 31px of text space for 27–28px values, enough to keep every number on one line with a little breathing room. The station column needs more width than the months because 'Station' and names like 'Riverside' are 65px unbreakable, but 100px is enough to establish row-header hierarchy without letting the label column dominate. r3A uses the full 725px measure exactly and keeps all twelve months identical, which is why it edges out the otherwise close r2A and r1A.

general: Columns that play the same role—especially repeated numeric measures—should normally share a width; unequal widths should encode a real grouping or priority.
Set each column's minimum from its longest unbreakable content plus padding, then spend remaining width where it improves scanning rather than distributing it arbitrarily.
A row-header column should be visibly wider than data columns but not so wide that it becomes the table's dominant feature.
Avoid lone wider columns at the end or periodic wider columns unless the content genuinely differs; readers infer structure from width.
specific: The twelve months are equivalent measures, so 52px each is the right rhythm; the 3–5px variations in r1C and r2C read as accidental noise.
With 725px and thirteen columns, the budget is tight: months can only range roughly 50–52px before the total exceeds the measure, while the station column can range about 88–100px.
An 88px station column leaves only 2px of slack around the 65px header and names, so it is usable but visibly tighter than the rest of the table.

tradeoffs: A designer could reasonably prefer r2A's 96px station column for a slightly more generous label-to-data ratio, or r3A's 100px for maximum label comfort and an exact 725px fill; the difference is small. One could also argue r2B's 88px station column is acceptable because it still fits, even though it looks cramped.
uncertain: Whether the 3–4px month-width differences in r1C and r2C are noticeable enough to count as faults rather than harmless variation, and whether a 112px station column (r3B) crosses from generous into disproportionate.

critique.good: Everything stays on one line, no header wraps, no mid-word splits; the month columns are perfectly uniform so the twelve months read as one even sequence, and the table nearly fills the 725px measure (723). The station column is clearly separated from the data field, so row identification is unambiguous.
critique.problems: The station column is over-generous while the numeric columns are starved: 'Riverside'/'Station' sit in 89px of text for a 65px word, leaving a conspicuous dead gutter after the names, yet each month gets only 30px for 28px of digits, so values like 24.1 sit about 1px from the cell rule. The result reads as 'wide label, squeezed numbers' — the eye is pulled to the empty space at the left instead of to the values being compared.
critique.cause: Col 1 was given 110px (≈24px surplus) and the 12 month columns only 51px (2px surplus each). Shifting ~20px from col 1 to the months would have given every number 3–4px of breathing room with no loss to the station label.

critique.good: Very strong hierarchy: the station column unmistakably reads as the row key, months remain a uniform block, and all cells stay single-line.
critique.problems: This is the worst imbalance of the three. The station column is enormously padded (107px of text for a 65px word — 42px of surplus) while Jan and Dec get exactly 27px for 27px of content, i.e. zero slack; in the render '24.1' and '23.5' nearly touch the column rules and look cramped and clipped-in-waiting. The table is also only 715px wide, so 9px of the available measure is simply wasted.
critique.cause: Col 1 = 128px starves the edge months, which were set to 48px (= exact minimum 48). The 42px of col-1 surplus could have added ~3.5px to every month column and still left the station name comfortable.

critique.good: The best proportion of the three: months are the widest columns at 53–54px, so each value gets 32–33px of text and a comfortable 2–2.5px gap on both sides; the numeric field is calm and easy to scan vertically, and the table fills the measure exactly (725).
critique.problems: The station column is now the tightest thing on the page: 86px means exactly 65px of text for a 65px word, so 'Station' and 'Riverside' sit flush against the column divider while the numbers float in generous space. That inverts the intended hierarchy — the row key should be the most relaxed element, not the most constrained. There is also a pointless 1px irregularity (Apr = 53 vs 54 for the rest) that neither reads as a group nor helps any value.
critique.cause: Col 1 was set to its absolute minimum 86px; the surplus that would have given the labels 3–4px of slack was spent on month columns that already had enough.

critique.good: The month field reads as one continuous chronological band: 52/53px widths are effectively uniform, so nothing in the data area pulls the eye. The station column is visibly the widest and clearly the row key, all cells single-line, row rhythm perfectly even at 33px. Overall a clean, publication-ready grid.
critique.problems: The proportion between key and data is slightly off. The station column carries 25px of surplus space around a 65px name while each month column has only 3px of surplus around a 28px number, so the names float in air while the numbers sit nearly against the cell borders. The result feels simultaneously loose at the left and cramped across the middle 12 columns — the data field, which is what the reader is actually comparing, is the tightest part of the table.
critique.cause: Station 90 (65px content) versus months 52 (28px content). The slack was spent on the identifier column, not on the analytical field.

critique.good: The generous station column (98px) does the most important job well: it separates the row key from the numeric field with a clear band of white space, so a reader never confuses a station name with a data cell. Month grid is calm.
critique.problems: December is 59px, eight pixels wider than every other month, which invents a false emphasis on the last column and leaves the right edge of the table visibly ragged against the dashed boundary. Meanwhile the remaining months at 51px are the tightest of the three designs, and 5px of the available budget goes unused — the exact 5px that should have been spread across the cramped months instead of dumped into Dec.
critique.cause: The 8px anomaly at Dec (59 vs 51) plus an over-wide Station at 98; the scaling correction pushed the surplus into the last column rather than distributing it.

critique.good: Aims at something real — quarter structure in a 12-month sequence — and keeps every cell single-line with a sensible station column at 91px. The base rhythm of 52px is comfortable.
critique.problems: The quarter idea does not read. Widening Apr, Jul and Oct produces a 3-4px stutter that looks like rounding error or jitter rather than grouping, because the emphasis falls on the first month of each quarter while Jan (also a first month) is not widened — the pattern is internally inconsistent, so the eye finds no rule. Extra space in a centred cell also splits to both sides, so no clean group boundary forms anywhere. The table ends up looking unevenly spaced for no legible reason.
critique.cause: 55px applied to columns 5, 8 and 11 only, breaking the uniform 52px grid asymmetrically.

critique.good: Clean and calm. The 96px station column clearly dominates the 52px month columns, so the row key reads first; all labels and values stay on one line; the equal month widths make horizontal comparison direct.
critique.problems: The layout stops 4px short of the available measure, and the station column has only 10px of slack beyond the longest name. Neither is damaging, but the leftover width could go to the row key, which has the longest unbreakable content.
critique.cause: Widths sum to 720px (96 + 12×52), leaving 4px unused. The 96px station width gives 75px of text space for a 65px longest word.

critique.good: Fills the 725px measure exactly, all cells remain single-line, and the 53px month columns give the numbers generous breathing room.
critique.problems: The station column is visibly cramped: 'Riverside' and 'Westfield' sit close to the column edge. The row key loses authority while the month field is wider than necessary, so the table reads data-first rather than station-first.
critique.cause: Station is 88px, leaving only 67px of text space for a 65px longest word (2px slack). The surplus goes to the months at 53px (32px text for 28px content, 4px slack), inverting the intended hierarchy.

critique.good: Station at 90px is reasonably comfortable, all values fit on one line, and the table is close to the full measure at 723px.
critique.problems: The 51-51-56 rhythm creates false emphasis on Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec. Those columns look like special quarter-end fields, and the actual quarter boundaries are not clarified. The uneven widths disturb comparison across a homogeneous 12-month sequence.
critique.cause: The extra 5px is on the last month of each quarter. With left-aligned headers and right-aligned numbers, the wide columns enlarge the gap after their headers but the gap before their numbers, so the header row and data rows suggest different break points; the grouping never reads cleanly at the quarter boundary.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r1B.why: Station column holds every name on one line; the twelve month columns are equal, comfortably wide, and the table fills the available width. Rows scan cleanly and the header hierarchy is clear.

ref_auto.why: All headers and values stay on one line and rows remain intact, but the table stops well short of the available width, leaving a conspicuous empty band at right; month columns are at minimum width.

r1A.why: Same strong allocation as A: full station names, even month columns with breathing room, and the grid uses the full measure so the table reads as one balanced block.

r2A.why: Station names and month values stay intact; equal month columns and full-width use give steady rhythm and easy comparison across months.

r3A.why: Comfortable station column, even month widths, no wrapping, and the table fills the frame; the repeated monthly columns read as a coherent set.

ref_equal.why: The Station column is far too narrow, breaking every row header into fragments ('River side', 'Nort hgat e', 'East woo d') and making row heights uneven; the table no longer scans as rows.

raw.unsure: A, C, D and E look nearly identical at this scale; I cannot reliably distinguish sub-pixel differences in their month-width rounding.

ref_equal.why: The Station column is far too narrow: 'Riverside', 'Northgate', 'Harbor', 'Eastwood' and 'Airport' break into awkward fragments, row heights become uneven, and the row-header scan is badly disrupted.

r1B.why: All station names and month headers stay on one line; month columns are even and the outer margins are balanced. The Station column is slightly roomy, but this does not harm comparison.

r3A.why: Station is just wide enough for the longest label while the remaining width is distributed evenly across the months; dense but coherent. The right edge nearly touches the guide, making the margin tighter than in B or E.

ref_auto.why: Labels are intact and months are uniform, but the Station column is visibly over-wide for its content, leaving excess white space and slightly narrowing the data columns.

r1A.why: Station fits the longest name with minimal slack, month columns are equal and comfortably wide, and the outer margins are balanced; rows scan cleanly.

r2A.why: Very close to E: all labels stay intact, month widths are even and margins are clean; the Station column is a touch more generous, with no real readability cost.

raw.unsure: The B–F differences are only a few pixels in the Station column; I cannot verify exact widths, and C's right edge sitting almost on the dashed guide may be intentional rather than a flaw.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
